questions.q: Although King Josiah was only eight years old when he became king, what did he do during his reign that pleased Yahweh?
questions.a: He sought after God, he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem from the shrines, idols, and carved figures.

questions.q: How did Josiah cleanse Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: He destroyed the altars, broke the Asherah poles, carved figures, and cast metal figures and the dust he scattered on the graves. The bones of the priests he burned on their altars.

questions.q: What did Josiah do in the land of Israel before he returned to Jerusalem?
questions.a: He repeated the cleansing that he did in Judah and Jerusalem.

questions.q: Where did the money come from that would be used to repair the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: The money had been collected from the people of Jerusalem and entrusted to the high priest.

questions.q: To whom was the money distributed and for what was it used?
questions.a: Carpenters and builders bought stone and timber to repair the temple.

questions.q: What roles did the Levites play in the repair of the temple?
questions.a: Some were supervisors, secretaries, administrators, and gate guards; others were good musicians and directed the faithful workmen.

questions.q: What did the priest find when he brought out the money that had been brought into the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: The high priest found the book of the law of Yahweh that had been given through Moses.

questions.q: What did the king do after hearing the words of the law?
Why will God’s anger be poured out on the people and not cease?
questions.a: They have forsaken him by worshiping other gods as their ancestors had done.

questions.q: Because Josiah’s heart was tender, what happened when he humbled himself after hearing God’s words?
questions.a: God said he would give him peace, and he would not see any of the disasters that God would bring on the people and land.

questions.q: Why did Josiah have all the people, great and small, gather together?
questions.a: Josiah read to them from the book of the covenant.

questions.q: What covenant did Josiah make with Yahweh?
questions.a: He made a covenant before Yahweh to keep his commandments.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do to obey Josiah?
questions.a: They worshiped Yahweh and did not turn away from him.

commentary.text: —As the years of infancy cannot be useful to our fellow-creatures, our earliest youth should be dedicated to God, that we may not waste any of the remaining short space of life. Happy and wise are those who seek the Lord and prepare for usefulness at an early age, when others are pursuing sinful pleasures, contracting bad habits, and forming ruinous connexions. Who can express the anguish prevented by early piety, and its blessed effects? Diligent self-examination and watchfulness will convince us of the deceitfulness and wickedness of our own hearts, and the sinfulness of our lives. We are here encouraged to humble ourselves before God, and to seek unto him, as Josiah did. And believers are here taught, not to fear death, but to welcome it, when it takes them away from the evil to come. Nothing hastens the ruin of a people, nor ripens them for it, more than their disregard of the attempts made for their reformation. Be not deceived, God is not mocked. The current and tide of affections only turns at the command of Him who raises up those that are dead in trespasses and sins. We behold peculiar loveliness, in the grace the Lord bestows on those, who in tender years seek to know and to love the Saviour. Hath Jesus, the Day-spring from on high, visited you? Can you trace your knowledge of this light and life of man, like Josiah, from your youth? Oh the unspeakable happiness of becoming acquainted with Jesus from our earliest years!
